To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PD-L1 expression is not consistently increased in KRAS mutant cell line models of NSCLC treated with relevant inhibitors of MEK or AKTs.
PD-L1 expression is not consistent and unlikely to be an earlier mechanism of resistance to MEK or AKt inhibitors in KRAS-mutant adeno-NSCLS.
PD-L1 over-expression is not consistent and unlikely to be an important mechanism of resistance to MEK or AKTi inhibitors in KRAS mutated NSCLC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new treatments for cancer, and in particular the use of targeted treatments.
the role of PD-1/PD-L1 pathway in the context of lung cancer.
the development of new therapies for lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PD-L1 expression levels of the cell lines tested were stable under the experimental conditions and that the PD-LP1 expression levels of these cell lines were not affected by MEK or AKI inhibition.
PD-L1 over-expression is not an early mechanism of drug resistance in KRAS mutant NSCLC.
PD-L1 expression changes are unlikely to be an effective biomarker of resistance in this setting and that the use of such biomarker in clinical practice is unlikely.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of PD-L1 is not a reliable biomarker in KRAS mutant NSCLC and is not an early mechanism of acquired resistance to MEK and/or AKT inhibitors in these cell lines.
PD-L1 expression is unlikely to be a relevant early mechanism of resistance in KRAS mutant adenco-NSCLC when treated with MEK and AKTI inhibitors.
we have demonstrated that PD-L1 over expression in KRAS mutated cell lines in vitro is not a consistent phenomenon in the context of MEK and AKTi treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PD-L1 is not a good predictive marker in KRAS mutant adenosquamous cell carcinoma.
PD-L1 upregulation is not a consistent feature of KRAS mutant NSCLC treated with AKT or MEK inhibitors.
PD-L1 is not a consistent biomarker of response to MEK or AKTs inhibitors in KRAS mutated adeno-NSLC.
